links.outcome: Whether entropy-based uncertainty visualization tracks LLM diagnostic reasoning uncertainty across rounds in pilot cases
links.effect: Unconfounded cerebellar infarction case showed monotonic entropy decay from 2.15 to 1.74; ambiguous pneumothorax case had sustained high entropy (~2.41); acute cholangitis showed top-1 rank stagnation. Pilot only, three cases, no clinician outcomes.
links.quote: Pilot validation across representative emergency medicine scenarios demonstrated distinct topological and information-theoretic behaviors: unconfounded cases (cerebellar infarction) exhibited smooth geodesic progression toward the ground truth alongside monotonic Shannon entropy decay from 2.15 to 1.74; noisy environments with ambiguous findings (spontaneous pneumothorax) suffered from trajectory wandering, local minimum traps, and high sustained entropy (~2.41) due to insufficient repulsive weighting for negative evidence; and triage-conflicted cases (acute cholangitis) achieved precise geometric proximity to the true node but experienced top-1 rank stagnation because the model conflated acute severity triage (sepsis) with anatomical etiology.

unlisted_practices: Entropy-based, ISOMAP-projected visualization of LLM diagnostic reasoning trajectories across sequential diagnostic rounds
Dual-channel safety decoupling and non-linear repulsive weighting for negative evidence (proposed, untested)

screen.reason: The paper introduces a novel technical framework/architecture using Shannon entropy and ISOMAP to quantify and visualize dynamic epistemic uncertainty in clinical LLM reasoning, evaluated on representative emergency medicine case vignettes.
